CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
May 5, 2021 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s  Executive  Order  N-29-20(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf), please note that
members of the public will only be allowed to observe and address
the Planning Commission Meeting of May 5, 2021 at 7:00 P.M. by
telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/
   The above access options provide the public with the
  opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.
   However, members of the public who wish to orally address the
  Planning Commission must use the public access options noted
  below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 2253351# wait 2 seconds and press # again

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

    When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.
    If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute
  the sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from
  the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making
  public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on May 5, 2021, the
day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date
and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior to
close of the public hearing will be made part of the official public
record of the meeting.
[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on
Following Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda other
  than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Mark Walker,
  representing Comfort LA, for Special Use Permit No. 2020-
  013(SP-2020-013) to allow the on-site consumption of beer,
  wine and distilled spirits in an existing take-out
  restaurant on an approximately 8,044 square-foot,
  C-2(General Commercial) zoned property at 902 North La Brea
  Avenue.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm the categorical exemption EA-CE-2020-122; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2020-013,
  subject to 13 conditions, and/or add conditions as
  deemed appropriate.

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Kristen
  Roberts, representing Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers, for
  Special Use Permit No. 2021-005(SP-2021-005) to allow 1) new
  construction with a valuation that exceeds twenty thousand
  dollars ($20,000.00) and 2) outdoor dining within a new
  approximately  6,300  square-foot  two-story  fast  food
  restaurant with a drive-through on an approximately 55,200
  square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial)/Medical Enterprise
  Overlay zoned property at 401 South Prairie Avenue.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2021-035; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2021-005,
  subject to 20 conditions, and/or add conditions as
  deemed appropriate

6.  Commission Initiatives.

7.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

8.  Adjournment.

If you will require special accommodations, due to a disability,
please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230, One
Manchester Boulevard, Fourth Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood,
CA 90301. All requests for special accommodations must be received
48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s). "Si no entiende esta
noticia o si necesita más información, favor de llamar a este número
(310) 412-5230."

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of May 5, 2021 is
not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other agenda
item being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing
agenda item will automatically be continued to the next regular
Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing  materials  are  available  at
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4
and at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk during regular
business hours. If any additional documents are received for
distribution to the Planning Commission after publication of this
Agenda but before 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting, they will
be made available for public inspection at the following webpage
  2
 https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-
4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future
Commission meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission
agendas for public participation option procedures at that time.)

minutes_text:
MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, MAY 05, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Tuesday, May 5, 2021, in the City Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner David Rice, the meeting was called
to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECD Director
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated that Planning received a
comment letter for Item 5B and has been distributed and posted on-
line. She stated that staff has provided a proposed draft revised
resolution for Item 5B that has been distributed and posted on-
line.

Ms. Wilcox announced that Marissa Fewell who was previously an
Assistant Planner has been promoted to a Planner.

Ms. Wilcox announced that a new intern, Sean May, was brought on
board.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None

(5) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

5A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-013 (SP-2020-013)902 N. LA BREA
AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Mark Walker,
representing Comfort LA, for Special Use Permit No. 2020-013 (SP-
2020-013) to allow the on-site consumption of beer, wine and
distilled spirits in an existing take-out restaurant on an
approximately 8,044 square-foot, C-2 (General Commercial) zoned
property at 902 North La Brea Avenue.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff a question regarding the Census
Tract.
   Ms. Wilcox provided clarification on who establishes the
  Census Tract.
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 5, 2021

Commissioner Trejo asked staff a question regarding seating
arrangements in the restaurant.
  - Ms. Fewell clarified that the restaurant was take-out only
  with no waiters.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff a question regarding outdoor
dining.
  - Ms. Fewell clarified that there is no proposed outdoor
  dining.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff if there could be a condition that
there will be no outdoor dining or drinking.

  - Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant is available to answer
  that question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff a question regarding the
installation of security cameras.

  - Ms. Fewell stated that the applicant will be required to
  install the security cameras.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.

Mr. Mark Walker, spoke to the Planning Commission via telephone
regarding his project on 902 North La Brea Avenue.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant questions regarding being
located close to a school and selling beer, wine and distilled
sprits
  - Mr. Walker responded with information on being close to
  a school.

Commissioner Patrick asked a question regarding the parking.
  - Mr. Walker responded with the information regarding
  parking.

Commissioner Trejo asked a question regarding alcohol not being
drank outside of the establishment.
  - Mr. Walker responded..

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked a question regarding the
security cameras.
  - Mr. Walker responded with information about the security
  cameras.

Chairman Springs asked a question regarding the establishment
having space for dining on the inside.
  - Mr. Walker responded with information about being a
  takeout restaurant.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None

  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 5, 2021
Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final comments from the commissioners?

Hearing none Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm the
categorical exemption EA-CE-2020-122 and adopt the attached
resolution approving SP-2021-013, subject to 13 conditions,
and/or add conditions as deemed appropriate and was seconded by
Commissioner Trejo, that Resolution No. 1895

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR
  MARK WALKER, REPRESENTING COMFORT LA, TO ALLOW
  THE ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF BEER, WINE AND
  DISTILLED SPIRITS WITHIN AN EXISTING 1,900
  SQUARE-FOOT  TAKE-OUT  RESTAURANT  ON  AN
  APPORXIMATELY 8,000 SQUARE-FOOT, C-2 (GENERAL
  COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY LOACATED AT 902
  NORTH LA BREA AVENUE

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Mindy Wilcox explained the appeal process.

5B: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-005 (SP-2021-005), 401 SOUTH
PRAIRIE AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Kristen Roberts,
representing Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers, for Special Use
Permit No. 2021-005 (SP-20219-005) to allow 1) new construction
with a valuation that exceeds twenty thousand dollars ($20,000.00)
and 2) outdoor dining within a new approximately 6,300 square-foot
two-story fast food restaurant with a drive-through on an
approximately 55,200 square-foot, C-2) (General Commercial)
/Medical Enterprise Overlay zoned property at 401 South Prairie
Avenue.

Mindy Wilcox stated that Staff received one item of correspondence
from the public.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff a question regarding where the
third driving lane will be located and will there be use of a
handheld device.
   Mr. McCrumby responded with information on where the aisle
  will be and that the handheld tablets will be used.

  3
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 5, 2021

Commissioner Rice asked staff questions about the staffing
capacity for cars that are in line. He asked questions regarding
the parking circulation.
  - Mr. McCrumby responded that the applicant has stated that the
  maximum is fifty-one (51) cars and provided clarification on
  staffing and the parking circulation.

Commissioner Rice asked staff questions regarding Condition 9 of
the Resolution.
  - Ms. Wilcox responded with information regarding the previous
  condition.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.
   Ms. Kristen Roberts, representing Raising Cane’s Chicken
  Fingers, came forward and spoke to the Planning Commission
  regarding the project.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick stated  that  the  applicant  addressed  her
concerns about the traffic.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant if she had spoken to any of
the local property owners.
  - Ms. Roberts referred to Mr. David Bella who spoke regarding
  the Community outreach that took place.

Commissioner Rice asked a question regarding the justification for
staying open until 3:30am
  - Ms. Roberts responded with the information about their
  standard hours of operation.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant to clarify why they would
be open until 3:30am.
  - Ms. Roberts responded that this is the Company standard
  for California.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant why the location will not
have a kiosk.
  - Ms. Roberts responded and explained why it was not needed
  at this time.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant how will the customers going
into the restaurant be managed?
  - Ms. Roberts responded regarding the customer flow of
  traffic inside.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant about the closing
time of 3:30.
  - Ms. Roberts responded regarding the hours of operation.

Chairman Springs asked staff if there were any regulations for
this type of restaurant in regards to hours of operation for the
City.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that there is nothing in the code
  specifying hours.

  4
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 5, 2021

Chairman Springs asked the applicant about the long lines in the
drive-thru.

  - Ms. Roberts responded regarding the drive-thru and speed
  of service.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant about the hours of
operation.

  - Ms. Roberts responded regarding the hours of operation.

Chairman Springs asked Mr. Lewis questions about the hours of
operation.

  - Attorney Jeff Lewis responded regarding limiting hours.

Commissioners Trejo stated concerns about the traffic and noise
impact.

Commissioners Shaw-Williams asked if there were any other
businesses in Inglewood that stayed open until 3:30am.

  - Mr. McCrumby responded that some drive-thru restaurants
  are open twenty-four hours.
  - Ms. Wilcox responded regarding another restaurant that is
  open twenty-four hours.

  Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated that she is okay with the
  hours.

  Commissioner Rice expressed concerns about the crowd of people
  coming from the entertainment district and would like to
  restrict the dining area to 2:00 am.

  - Ms. Roberts responded about the hours of operation for
  other Raising Cane’s in surrounding cities.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final comments from the commissioners?

Commissioner Patrick asked about the opening date.

  - Ms. Roberts stated January 2022.

Hearing none Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-035 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2021-005, subject to 20 conditions, and/or add
conditions as deemed appropriate and add a 1 year review was
seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, that Resolution No.1896

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF  THE  CITY  OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw Williams and

Ms. Mindy Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(6) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None

Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

(8) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick –
 Wished everyone a happy Mother’s Day.

Commissioner Trejo-
 Did Code Enforcement go out to the auto repair at Century and
  Inglewood Ave?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that she will check in with them and follow-
  up with an update.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams-
 Wished everyone a happy Mother’s Day.

Chairman Springs-
 Concerns can be addressed as a resident of the city to the City
  Council in that district and to the Planning Commission.
 In the Hollywood Park tomorrow are there plans for sit-down
  restaurants?
  Ms. Wilcox stated yes.
 There is a committee that was put together by Councilman Dotson
  to discuss what should be developed in Hollywood Park Tomorrow.

  6

Chairman Springs wished everyone a happy Mother’s Day and a good
evening and adjourned the meeting.
